guide: This post is a personal introduction, so there is nothing to build from it directly. What you can do is turn your own background into a first small AI project and share it publicly. You need a ChatGPT or Claude account, a free Vercel account and one idea you care about.
1. Write three plain sentences in a note: who you are, what you do, and one thing you wish was easier in your work or hobby.
1. Pick that one thing as your first project, such as a small app for a hobby or a tool that saves your business a repetitive task.
1. Ask Claude Code or ChatGPT (Codex) to build the smallest working version, and tell it your three sentences so it knows who the project is for.
1. Put it online with Vercel so you can send people a link instead of a screenshot.
1. Add a simple page on the same site that says what you are building and what you have learned so far.
1. Share each small step as you finish it, and note what worked, what failed and what it cost you in AI subscriptions.
Watch out: do not wait until the project is polished or you have a big idea. Start with one small thing you care about, because that is what attracts people with the same interests.

```
You are a patient senior developer helping a beginner build and publish a first project. I am <your name>, I work in <your field or hobby>, and the problem I want to solve is <one thing that is slow or annoying>.
Build the smallest working version of a simple web app that solves this for <who will use it>. I have a <ChatGPT / Claude> account and a free Vercel account, and I am not an experienced coder. Use common, well-documented tools such as Next.js and avoid anything that needs a paid service.
Constraints: keep it to one main feature, explain each step in plain English, and tell me exactly what to run or click next. Do not ask me to paste secrets into the chat; show me how to store them as environment variables.
Return: 1) a short plan in no more than five steps, 2) the full code for each file with its file name, 3) the commands to run it locally, 4) step-by-step instructions to deploy it on Vercel, and 5) a simple "about this project" page I can add, with placeholders for what I have learned.
```
